newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS SEEN DOWN, LACK CONFIDENCE IN ECONOMY.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS SEEN DOWN, LACK CONFIDENCE IN ECONOMY.

text.p: Thai stocks were seen continuing to fall on Thursday as investors did not have full confidence in the government's restrictive economic measures announced earlier this week, brokers said.

"Investors are watching how those economic measures announced by the government on Tuesday can really remedy the economic problems. Now it's up to the government to show to investors that the measures are practical and could solve problems,' said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance.
The composite SET index closed 13.15 points lower at 635.32 on about five billion baht turnover on Wednesday.
In a bid to salvage the ailing economy, the government on Tuesday suspended operations of 42 troubled finance companies, bringing to the total of 58 finance companies suspended since late June.
The suspension of finance companies had caused a run on deposits at some banks and finance companies on Wednesday.
The government hopes to receive $12-$15 billion in loans from the International Monetary Fund and foreign countries if the austerity measures are carried out properly.
